# - Compressed data
# - UPX footer at the end

retrieved_cards.title: Inline data or junk bytes can be rendered as instructions
retrieved_cards.applicability_signal: Bytes that are actually data (jump tables, constants, padding) or deliberate junk are being decoded and read as executable instructions.
retrieved_cards.mechanism: The boundary between code and data is ambiguous to the tool; non-code bytes decoded as instructions create spurious logic that never executes.
retrieved_cards.validation_note: Check how the region is referenced (branched to, vs loaded as data) and whether any control-flow edge reaches it; a region with only data references is not code.
retrieved_cards.misleading_interpretation: These decoded instructions are real code, so they participate in the logic.
retrieved_cards.better_interpretation: Confirm a control-flow edge reaches the region as code, rather than it being referenced as data, before reversing it.
not_applicable_when: the region is confirmed to be the target of a control-flow edge
the bytes are clearly referenced as data
misfire_risks: genuine code can look data-like; base the call on references and reachability, not on the bytes looking unusual
minimum_evidence_before_use: a region decoded as instructions has data-like or junk characteristics

retrieved_cards.title: A function's name asserts behaviour the code may not perform
retrieved_cards.applicability_signal: A function carries a semantically loaded name -- one that asserts it validates, compares, decrypts or decides -- and is being trusted to be the gate or to do what its name says, without confirming its actual behaviour.
retrieved_cards.mechanism: A symbol name is conflated with the function's actual semantics; names are author-chosen labels and can be wrong, stale, or deliberately misleading.
retrieved_cards.validation_note: Read the body to confirm behaviour matches the name, then follow its return value forward: a check whose result the accepting branch does not consume is not the gate, however correct its comparison is.
retrieved_cards.misleading_interpretation: The function does what its name says (it is the validator / it decrypts the flag), so reverse it directly.
retrieved_cards.better_interpretation: Treat the name as a hint, not a fact; confirm what the function actually computes and whether the accept path uses its result.
not_applicable_when: the function's behaviour has been confirmed to match its name
